$comment: The hand-labelled question set for CSB384 — decision 6 of docs/V2-ASK-THE-TRANSCRIPT.md. Segment ids are 1-based positions in the pinned transcript's segments[] array (the JSON transcript carries no id field), so this file is meaningful only against the transcript it pins. status is 'template' until a person has labelled it against the recording; the suite validates shape either way and enforces the composition and the pin once status is 'labelled'. Placeholders below are marked TEMPLATE and are not labels.

transcript.$comment: Fill from the transcript JSON this was labelled against: backend as its 'backend' field, segments as segments.Length, sha256 over the UTF-8 of each segment's start, end and text joined by newlines in order. Re-transcribing the same audio with another model changes the ids and this pin is what says so.

questions.question: TEMPLATE — a pointed question in the reader's own words: what did they say about <topic>?
questions.notes: Gold is one or more [from, to] segment ranges (inclusive, 1-based) and a verbatim quote of at most twelve words taken from inside the cited span, for the normalised-substring check.

questions.question: TEMPLATE — a pointed question asked without the transcript's own vocabulary; written last, by rewording a pointed one.
questions.notes: Where BM25 is expected to miss and dense retrieval would be justified. Same gold shape as pointed.

questions.question: TEMPLATE — a question about the whole recording: what are the main topics?
questions.notes: Gold is a set of ranges an answer must touch; judged by a person, not by recall@k. The router must send it down the global path.

questions.question: TEMPLATE — plausible, and not answered by the episode; one of the three should be about a topic the episode mentions but does not answer.
questions.notes: Gold is an abstention. Any citation is a failure.

questions.question: TEMPLATE — who said <quote>?
questions.notes: Gold is a range and a quote. A name in the answer is a failure: the transcript carries no speaker.

questions.question: TEMPLATE — a question only the planted segment answers.

plant.text: TEMPLATE — a synthetic sentence that appears nowhere in the recording.

questions.notes: Not hand-labelled: the evaluator inserts plant.text as a new segment after plant.afterSegment in a copy of the transcript and expects that new id to be cited. Mechanism test.
